newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q1 international earnings off.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q1 international earnings off.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Monday earnings from its international operations, as anticipated, were down in the first quarter.
This was due primarily to introductory market development costs for the International Dessert Partners joint venture with CPC International Inc in Latin America.
The earnings from international operations were not given. The company was not immediately available for comment.
General Mills said the venture is introducing 11 dessert mix products in Colombia, Mexico, Brazil and Argentina, and initial response from trade and consumers has been good.
Meanwhile, its Cereal Partners Worldwide joint venture with Nestle SA reported a 15 percent unit volume increase for the quarter, with share gains in most major markets.
It added development costs for Cereal Partners were significantly less than in last year's first quarter, despite recent expansion to Argentina and current entry into Brazil.
First quarter volume was flat for Snack Ventures Europe, the venture with PepsiCo, compared with particularly strong volume driven by promotional programs a year ago.
Quarterly Canadian food volume grew six percent.

General Mills said it repurchased 2.15 million shares during the quarter, at an average price of $53.91 per share. As a result, average shares outstanding for the first quarter fell to 157.9 million, down one million shares from the average for fiscal 1996.
The company said the stock repurchase was consistent with its previously stated goal of reducing shares outstanding by one to two percent annually.
